commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a Telegram-specific href escaper that leaves raw ampersands in link attributes, updates formatter regression tests, and adds a formatter proof script.

PR surface: Source +13, Tests +18, Other +75. Total +106 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. by source inspection: current main linkifies Telegram markdown/rich bare URLs and escapes href/text through the existing Telegram HTML escaping path. I did not perform a live Telegram tap test in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Human follow-up is needed because the remaining blockers are maintainer scope direction and real Telegram client proof, not a safe autonomous repair lane.

target.title: fix(telegram): links with '&' query params drop parameters when tapped (#102162) [AI-assisted]
target.body: > [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code. Closes #102162 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where operators using the Telegram channel would tap a link in a model reply and land on the wrong page. Any bare URL whose query string contains multiple parameters separated by `&` — e.g. `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit` — was sent to the Telegram client with the `&` HTML-escaped to `&` inside the `` attribute. Telegram's Bot API HTML parser does **not** decode `&` in attribute values, so the "Open link?" prompt and the resulting navigation carry `&action=edit` literally, and every parameter after the first `&` (`action=edit`) is dropped. The server then falls back to a default page instead of the intended destination. ## Why This Change Was Made `buildTelegramLink` in `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` escaped the link href through `escapeHtmlAttr`, which encodes `&` → `&`. That encoding is technically valid HTML for an attribute, but Telegram's lenient HTML parser treats it literally, breaking multi-parameter URLs. This change adds a dedicated `escapeTelegramLinkHref` helper used only for link hrefs. It keeps the query `&` raw (so the URL stays navigable) and only escapes the characters that could actually break out of a double-quoted attribute (`"`, `<`, `>`). A raw `&` is safe inline inside a double-quoted attribute. The visible bubble text of an auto-link still carries `&`, which is correct: Telegram **does** decode standard entities in text content, so the bubble renders the URL properly. Only the attribute-decoding path was broken, so only the href needed changing. No other caller of `escapeHtmlAttr` (code-language classes, image `src`) is affected. ## User Impact Operators tapping a multi-parameter link in a Telegram message now reach the exact destination the model sent (`?post=100&action=edit`), instead of having every parameter after the first `&` silently dropped. Plain single-parameter URLs and `[label](url)` markdown links are unchanged. ## Evidence Real behavior proof captured by running the **production** formatter (`markdownToTelegramHtml` legacy mode + `markdownToTelegramRichHtml` rich mode) on a bare URL with a multi-parameter query string, via `pnpm exec tsx scripts/proof/telegram-url-amp-proof.mjs`. This exercises the actual code path (not a mocked harness) on `current upstream/main`. **Before the fix** (unpatched `format.ts`) — the `&` is encoded to `&` in the href, so the link is not navigable: ``` Input bare URL: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit --- markdownToTelegramHtml (legacy HTML mode) --- emitted html: See https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit for details. [legacy] href attr : https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit [legacy] href navigable : NO (broken) --- markdownToTelegramRichHtml (rich HTML mode) --- [rich] href attr : https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit [rich] href navigable : NO (broken) RESULT: BUG PRESENT — encodes '&' as '&' and drops params. ``` **After the fix** — the href keeps the raw `&` separator and is navigable in both HTML modes: ``` --- markdownToTelegramHtml (legacy HTML mode) --- emitted html: See https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit for details. [legacy] href attr : https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit [legacy] text has & : yes (ok: Telegram decodes text content) [legacy] href navigable : YES --- markdownToTelegramRichHtml (rich HTML mode) --- [rich] href attr : https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit [rich] href navigable : YES RESULT: FIXED — keeps the query '&' raw and is navigable. ``` Regression test added in `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts` (`keeps '&' raw in link hrefs so multi-param URLs stay navigable (#102162)`), asserting the href stays raw for bare URLs, `[label](url)` links, and rich HTML mode. Full `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts` suite: **69 passed** (was 68 + 1 new). Scoped typecheck (`tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`) and `oxlint` on the changed files are clean. ## Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / cleanup ## Scope - [x] `extensions/telegram` (channel formatter) ## Security Impact - Does this change authentication, authorization, or trust boundaries? **No.** - Does this change how secrets, tokens, or credentials are handled? **No.** - Does this change any security boundary (sandbox, network egress, prompt isolation)? **No.** - Does this introduce any new external data ingestion or code execution? **No.** - Does this change logging or telemetry that could leak sensitive data? **No.** This only relaxes HTML-attribute escaping for the `&` character inside Telegram link hrefs. It cannot break out of the double-quoted attribute (only `"` is quote-escaped for that), and hrefs come from already-validated link spans. ## Human Verification Verified via the real-source `tsx` proof above that the production formatter emits a navigable href in both legacy and rich HTML modes, before (broken) and after (fixed). Verified the existing 68 formatter tests still pass (no regression) plus the new regression test. Edge cases checked: bare auto-linked URL, `[label](url)` markdown link, and rich HTML mode all keep the href raw. **Not tested:** a live Telegram client end-to-end (no bot token in this environment). The formatter output is deterministic and the href is now byte-for-byte the navigable URL; Telegram's attribute handling is the documented root cause per #102162. macOS/iOS Telegram client variations not exercised. ## Compatibility / Migration Backward compatible. URLs that previously rendered with `&` in the href (which Telegram could not navigate) now render with a raw `&` and navigate correctly. No config or API surface changes. URLs without `&` in the query string are byte-identical to before. ## Failure Recovery Revert the single commit. The change is isolated to one helper call site in `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts` (`escapeHtmlAttr` → `escapeTelegramLinkHref` in `buildTelegramLink`); reverting restores the prior `&` href behavior. ## Risks and Mitigations - **Raw `&` in an HTML attribute is technically not strict HTML.** Mitigation: Telegram's Bot API HTML parser is lenient and is exactly the reason `&` broke (it does not decode entities in attributes). Raw `&` is the pragmatic standard for URL query separators in HTML hrefs and is what Slack and other channels emit. The attribute cannot be broken out of (only `"` is escaped for boundary safety). - **A URL containing a literal `"`** would be escaped to `"`. Such characters are invalid in URLs (they must be percent-encoded), so linkify will not produce them; non-issue in practice.
